chunks: And he narrated from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ and Sindī ibn Muḥammad, both from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Saʿīd ibn Yasār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A woman is prohibited from salat (prayer), then she becomes pure and performs wudu (ablution) without performing ghusl (ritual bath); may her husband approach her before she performs ghusl? He said: “No, not until she performs ghusl.”

So it is to be understood as meaning that it is preferable that he not approach her, and more virtuous that he leave her until she performs ghusl, without that being prohibited—such that if he were to have intercourse with her before she performs ghusl, he would not be sinful. That which clarifies this is as follows.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), which is suspended during menstruation
key_terms.الْأَفْضَلَ: the more virtuous or preferable course

ai.seo_question: Can a husband have intercourse with his wife after her menses ends but before she performs ghusl (ritual bath)?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling on a husband approaching his wife after her menstruation has ended but before she has performed ghusl (ritual bath). The wording indicates withholding until ghusl, while the appended legal clarification explains the instruction as indicating what is more preferable rather than strict prohibition.
